typography.headingCharacter: Geometric-leaning grotesque, double-storey a, straight-cut descenders, tall x-height, medium weight, slightly tight tracking, sentence case, leading close to 1.1
typography.bodyCharacter: Same grotesque at regular weight, normal tracking, generous ~1.5 leading, measure held to roughly 45 characters so it wraps well short of the artwork

composition.structure: Full-bleed illustrated canvas with the interface floated on top: wordmark top-left, a segmented nav cluster pinned top-right, all hero copy stacked on a single left rail in the flat sky region. The right half is left to the artwork, with status chips overlapping it.

spacing.rhythm: Large uninterrupted emptiness in the upper-left sky; tight grouping inside clusters (heading to subhead, button pair, chip stack) with big gaps between those clusters. Nav items pack close together.

surfaceTreatment.finish: A hard-edged pixel raster backdrop with no antialiasing, overlaid by smooth dark translucent chrome — nav segments and status chips tinted so the scene reads through them — plus one opaque warm-white button

imagery.treatment: 16-bit pixel-art landscape as the entire hero canvas, bled to all four edges, unframed and uncropped; product state is implied by floating chips rather than screenshots

motion.character: Hero arrives once on load over 600ms on a near-expo curve; micro-states (colour, opacity, border) flip in 20-120ms; carets blink on steps(1) at 0.9-1s and a 2.8s shimmer loops. Buttons only shift background on hover.
motion.choreography: Script-driven rather than CSS-declared: hundreds of elements carry inline transform/opacity, ~79 move at a rate other than the scroll (parallax or pinning), 8 fade in and 3 scale, and reveals land at several distinct depths rather than as one batch. Header sticks and resizes.

philosophy.text: The argument is that an AI operations product can be introduced as a place rather than a dashboard: a sunlit pixel-art park, drawn coarse enough to read as a game world, doing the job a gradient or a product screenshot normally does. Everything functional is then treated as an overlay guest — smooth translucent dark chrome, one warm-white pill, hairline-divided nav segments — so the interface never competes with the art, and the only place text can sit is the empty sky at upper left. That is the trade: half the frame is surrendered to atmosphere and the copy is confined to a single narrow rail, buying charm and memorability at the cost of hierarchy and density. Credibility is smuggled back in through motion craft rather than layout — scroll-linked parallax across dozens of elements, sequenced reveals at staggered depths, blinking carets that make the scene feel live, and a genuine reduced-motion fallback that withdraws most of it for anyone who asks.

build.techniques: Full-bleed pixel-art canvas with floating UI overlaid; timeline-sequenced staggered reveals across 3+ depth layers; script-driven parallax on ~79 elements at non-scroll rates; micro-state flips (20–120ms) on button hover; shimmer loop (2.8s) and step-blink carets (0.9–1s) via precise animation intervals; sticky header with resize callback.
